royal-niger-company.description: Badge: a black Y for the Niger, the Benue and their joined course to the sea, with ARS, JUS and PAX in yellow on its arms, inside a red ring on white. Flown on a White Ensign from 2 June 1887, then on a Blue Ensign from 1 February 1888.
royal-niger-company.note: Its use until 1899 is presumed, not documented.

colonial-badges.actor: Lagos Colony, the Oil Rivers and Niger Coast Protectorates, Northern and Southern Nigeria
colonial-badges.description: Badges existed and are listed by flag reference sites.
colonial-badges.note: No source checked so far describes them, so none is drawn yet.

nigeria-1914.description: Blue Ensign with a red disc holding a green six-pointed star around a crown, with "Nigeria" below. Lugard wrote in 1940 that he first suggested the star design, for Northern Nigeria.
nigeria-1914.note: A change to St Edward's Crown after 1953 is a theory, and one writer is not sure those versions flew, so they are not used.

nana-olomu.description: Two personal flags, both made before 1894. One is red with a printed Union Flag in the corner and NANNA in white. The other is yellow with an upside-down Union Flag, NANNA in blue and a painted man shooting a leopard; it was captured in 1894.
nana-olomu.note: Local images next to a printed Union Flag: the mix says something about delta politics in the 1880s.

unidentified-1897.description: Red, with white figures of one man beheading another. Said to have been brought back from the 1897 Benin expedition.
unidentified-1897.disputed: Its maker, owner and meaning are unknown. It is shown only as an unidentified flag, never as Benin's.

benin-leopard.description: The leopard, one of the principal symbols of the Oba in Benin court art. Coral-bead regalia, mudfish and ivory trumpets also mark kingship.
benin-leopard.note: A royal symbol, not a flag: no flag of the kingdom is documented. Drawn as a plain silhouette, not copied from objects taken in 1897. The source checked does not date the leopard imagery.

yoruba-knot.actor: Yoruba kingdoms (Ife, Oyo and their successors)
yoruba-knot.description: The interlaced Solomon's knot, commonly viewed as a royal symbol among the Yoruba.

dagin-arewa.description: The Dagin Arewa, a star-shaped northern knot used in building, design and embroidery.
dagin-arewa.note: Its age is not known from the sources checked, so it is not yet placed in any century. No city flags are documented.

sokoto-caliphate.description: Flags circulate online, but no source for any design has been found.
sokoto-caliphate.note: Nothing is drawn until a description from the time or a surviving banner is found, for example in travellers' accounts such as Clapperton's or Barth's.

kanem-bornu.description: Flags shown online for Kanem and Bornu have no source.
kanem-bornu.note: The palm-tree flag shown for Kanem traces to the imaginary kingdom of "Organa" on 14th-century European maps. It is never used.

aro.description: A flag with crowns, a musket and a lance is shown online without a source.
aro.note: It may be a modern community flag. Nothing is drawn until its origin is checked.

nri-igbo.description: No emblem is documented in the sources checked for the communities represented here.
nri-igbo.note: Ichi facial marks showed status, not political rule, and are not used as decoration.

biafra.description: Red, black and green stripes with a golden rising sun of eleven rays, one for each province, over a gold bar. First raised on 30 May 1967, taken from the Eastern Region's arms.

nigeria-1960.description: Green-white-green, designed by Michael Taiwo Akinkunmi and chosen in 1959 from almost 3,000 entries. His red sun was removed. Raised at midnight on 1 October 1960.
